findings.conclusion: Selection reuses existing sqlite3_complete boundaries, classifier and name helper, without changing their bodies. For the fixed canonical source both requested unquoted lowercase definitions match exactly once; caller order, complete original SQL and partial WHERE predicate are retained. Trigger-contained SQL text and unrelated index are not selected.

A repeated requested literal name, missing exact definition or repeated exact definition returns None. All statements are collected before returning; caller applies ? before execute_batch, so selection failure executes no maintenance DDL.

OnceLock<Option<String>> retains only a compiled immutable SQL-selection result, including deterministic failure. It does not retain a Connection, generation, snapshot or DB existence state. Every matching-schema invocation still executes the two DDL statements and then unchanged read_generation::ensure.

Version25, full canonical schema, fresh initialization and mismatch behavior remain unchanged. The added selected SQL contains only the original two CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements; no new DML, PRAGMA, row/epoch/incarnation update is introduced. Existing read_generation::ensure behavior is preserved, not claimed DML-free in all circumstances.

Existing test now drops both maintained indexes, preserves the query_only refusal plus typed row/metadata snapshot, reopens twice and compares every sqlite_schema definition to the fresh original. Existing indexed FK-cascade plan and real delete assertions remain.

limitations: The unchanged classifier/name helper is not a generic SQLite identifier parser. It recognizes current canonical line comments and exact unquoted names; this review does not certify arbitrary quoted/schema-qualified identifiers, leading block comments, or case-varied duplicate spellings. Missing exact current definitions fail closed; no universal SQL-identifier duplicate guarantee is asserted.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS still does not repair an already present incorrectly defined index; that is unchanged prior behavior, not a new regression.
No deterministic current-source bug or mandatory patch was found statically. No performance gain is claimed; one-time SQL splitting is added and then cached.
The 11+5+5=21 tests are source-defined nonignored methods, not executed passes.
